dossier.architecture: Compact turret with omnidirectional note feed and lightweight auxiliary endgame.

subsystems.drivetrain: Narrow SDS modules create room for the note path; module standoffs help define the feeder cage.
subsystems.intake: Under-bumper intake feeds four vertical rollers.
subsystems.transfer: Rotating rollers draw the note around the cage into the turret at different headings.
subsystems.scoring: Continuously aiming turret; lightweight amp bar guides an upward shot.
subsystems.endgame: Late-added light climber uses a worm drive to resist backdrive.
subsystems.controls: Turret-mounted Limelight requires moving-camera pose transforms; superstructure states coordinate mechanisms.

versions: Conceptual feed prototype validated before detailed design. Climber added after prioritizing the main scoring architecture.
dossier.analysis: A turret is useful only if its feed remains viable across turret headings. Narrow modules and a shared cage are enabling packaging choices, not incidental component preferences.
limits: Only source-established configurations and changes are described; intermediate revisions may remain unresolved.

context_documents.body:
# 2024-2910: Any-heading note loading is the prerequisite for a useful turret

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Under-bumper acquisition feeds four vertical rollers that move the note around the turret’s receiving cage. A light amp guide directs an upward release. The source describes a late, simple worm-drive climb and software superstates that coordinate turret, feeder and launcher rather than binding unrelated commands independently.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly emphasizes feeding at different turret headings. Climb packaging was constrained by its late addition, motivating simplicity and low mass.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A turret adds little directional independence if it must return to one heading to acquire every note. The receiving cage and its contact sequence are therefore as important as aiming range. A superstate helps express the common readiness condition, but needs fault handling when only some mechanisms reach their setpoints. A worm transmission should not be assumed to hold every load without checking its actual efficiency and disabled behavior.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure transfer success versus heading, note wear and acceleration. Test partial readiness, cable limits and power-off climb retention. The viewer-disabled binder remains unreviewed; do not substitute a guessed download.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation
